# Commercial Analysis

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. Commercial analysis structures judgement about a market, it does not validate it: the thesis it tests can still fail, private equity carries a real risk of loss, and no memo here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the commercial analysis skill of the private equity pack in andreworia/claude-finance-skills. Use it during the commercial diligence workstream, typically weeks two to four of a process, on any business whose thesis depends on market growth, competitive positioning or adjacent expansion; it structures the framework that primary customer reference interviews should test, and does not replace them. The method defines the market first with a substitution test (what would a buyer choose if this company did not exist), stated at vertical, horizontal adjacency and geographic levels in one anchor sentence, because vague definitions inflate TAM. Sizing then runs top-down from named, attributable data filtered to SAM and SOM, cross-checked bottom-up by buyer count times realistic spend, with divergence beyond two to three times treated as a flaw to investigate, and the claimed growth rate tested against new entrants, public company growth and the company own spend trend. Porter Five Forces is applied to this company in this market, not the sector generically: entrant barriers and time to parity, buyer power and switching costs, supplier dependence and single-source...
